newsitem.title: USA: Florida seeks federal disaster declaration.
newsitem.headline: Florida seeks federal disaster declaration.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles has asked that President Clinton declare 15 counties federal disaster areas for damage caused when Tropical Storm Josephine crossed the state last week, a spokeswoman for the governor said Sunday.
In a letter to the president, Chiles said that Josephine, which made landfall on Florida's northern Gulf Coast Oct. 7, was the ninth major disaster to hit Florida since March 1993.
The storm has been blamed for only one death in Florida, an elderly woman killed Oct. 10 when a tree damaged by the storm toppled on her.

Florida sustained some wind damage and heavy flooding associated with Josephine, with some areas reporting 13 inches (33 cm) of rain. More than 130,000 people lost power and about 1,920 people stayed in shelters, some for as long as three days, Chiles said.
The counties affected by Chiles' request are Taylor, Dixie, Duval, Hillsborough, Pasco, Pinellas, Putnam, Sarasota, Volusia, Levy, Citrus, Hernando, Baker, Clay and Manatee.
